scenes.narration: The bleak reading of Space Runaway Ideon is also the most testable one. Legendary Giant Ideon, also The Ideon) is a 1980 anime television series produced by Nippon Sunrise, created and directed by Yoshiyuki Tomino, produced immediately following his signature work, Mobile Suit Gundam. It first premiered on Tokyo Channel 12 from 1980 to 1981, followed by two feature films in 1982.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Space Runaway Ideon. The television series credited only the design studio, while Higuchi received full credit for the subsequent films. The series won the Animage Anime Grand Prix prize for the second half of 1980.

The self that experiences Space Runaway Ideon is a committee, not a king. Space Runaway Ideon begins in 2300, far enough in the future that mankind has begun colonizing other planets. On the planet Solo in the Andromeda Galaxy, a group of archaeologists have come across the mysterious remains of the Ideon—three large armored tanks with the ability to combine into a godlike mecha.

Reproduction explains more of Space Runaway Ideon than any philosophy dares to admit. For six months, they have diligently restored the machines, but have failed to get the giant tanks to move. Suddenly, a humanoid alien civilization known as the Buff Clan comes across Solo.

Once you see Space Runaway Ideon as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Assuming the "aliens" (Earthling colonists) have attacked Karala, the Buff Clan begins to attack. Cosmo Yuki, the afro-wearing protagonist of the series, and his friends Kasha Imhof and Deck Afta climb aboard the three tanks, which activate on their own, and, when they initially combine to form the Ideon, fend off the first assault, repelling Gije's men.

The story Space Runaway Ideon tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. This is a short respite, though, as another force is sent down soon after. Bes Jordan, leader of the sparse military force stationed on Solo, orders that the Ideon tanks be armed with missiles, but while this is happening, the cities on Solo are obliterated by Buff Clan soldiers.

Meaning is not found in Space Runaway Ideon — it is manufactured for it. Gije and his partner Damido, meeting up with the leader of their expedition, Abadidi Gurimade, soon launch more attacks on the planet Solo in an attempt to capture the Ideon (which they refer to as the 'Giant God'). The survivors flee inside the Solo Ship and Karala and Mayaya, who are mistaken by Bes as colonists, are let onboard as well.

The cold light on Space Runaway Ideon leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Other civilians who quickly get onboard the Solo Ship include Sheryl Formosa, a linguist studying the civilization on Solo; Sheryl's sister, Lin; Banda Lotta; three children: Piper Lou, Ashura Nobaku, and Fard Maraka; mechanic Joliver Ira, pilot Hatari Naburu; and Moera Fatima. The pilots Tekuno and Bento soon join Cosmo and Kasha as pilots of the Ideon's 3 parts and Moera soon replaces Bes as another pilot.

Space Runaway Ideon did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. Karala and Mayaya are soon discovered to be aliens, and while Mayaya is killed, Bes has taken a liking to Karala and she is allowed to live, although Sheryl and others distrust her. Karala tells everyone of the Legend of Ide, a story of the Buff Clan's savior, who saved them with the power of the Ide.

The honest version of Space Runaway Ideon starts by giving up the comforting part. The Buff Clan have searched the universe for this legendary existence, which is what powers both the Ideon and the Solo Ship. The Solo Ship soon flees Solo using its powerful DS Drive engines and, after a fight in sub space with the Buff Clan, arrives at the planet Saurus Star.

Strip Space Runaway Ideon of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Bes, Cosmo, and the others confront Gije in a powerful Dogg Mack Mobile Suit and later in man to man fighting. Abadidi receives orders from above - Karala's elder sister Harulu - that they no longer have to worry about harming Karala and can kill her if they need to, since she has shamed the Ajiba family by associating with the humans.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Space Runaway Ideon shows exactly where that breaks. The Buff Clan force chases the Solo Ship to the planet Crystal Star, where Abadidi heads out himself in a Dogg Mack. His attempts to destroy the Solo Ship with giant winged creatures known as Bajins backfires and it is he who is killed by them.

What looks like free choice in Space Runaway Ideon is older than choice itself. With Abadidi dead and Damido injured, Harulu herself heads to the front. Arriving on the planet Ruins Star, Karala tries to make peace with her sister, but is humiliated by Harulu's underlings.

Nobody designed the part of Space Runaway Ideon you experience — it was inherited. Things get even worse for her when Banda Lotta, upset by all the harm the Buff Clan has caused, tries to kill her, but folds under pressure. Karala, who is willing to die, impresses everyone on the Solo Ship with her strength.

Every serious account of Space Runaway Ideon eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. The Solo Ship arrives at an Earth base where Cosmo meets Camyula, a female officer who reminds him of his mother. Damido, now recovered, makes one final attempt to destroy the Ideon, but is killed as well.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Space Runaway Ideon — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. The Solo Ship heads to the planet Ajian, and when Gije attacks the planet, the Ideon uses its powerful Black Hole Cannon, which prevents the Buff Clan's missiles from hitting the planet, but ends up destroying a lot of the planet as a result. Gije heads back to the Buff Clan homeworld as the Solo Ship travels to the planet Flag Star.

The selfish-gene reading of Space Runaway Ideon makes it less romantic and far more precise. The Solo Ship and Harulu's Dorowa Zan meet in space and the Dorowa is destroyed. Harulu flees in an escape capsule and meets up with Daram Zuba, a former lover and member of the Ome Foundation, which is plotting with Doba to overthrow the Buff Clan Emperor.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. With Gije with him, Daram now becomes the main adversary of the Solo Ship as it goes to the planet Kyaral. There, Cosmo meets Kitty Kitten, who desires for the Solo Ship to flee, since it will bring nothing but more heartbreak to their wartorn planet.

The feeling that Space Runaway Ideon means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. Kitty is shot to death soon after by Daram and Cosmo is injured, saved only by a blood transfusion from Karala. The Solo Ship, still pursued by Daram, approaches Earth, but the crew and the survivors learn that their fellow Earthlings will not welcome them.

Nothing in Space Runaway Ideon was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Sheryl and Joliver head to the moon to use the Earth military's powerful Gloria computer and discover that the power of Ide is infinite. The Solo Ship is attacked yet again and the Ideon uses its newest weapon, the Ideon Gun, to defend itself.

The psychology underneath Space Runaway Ideon is simpler and older than the story on top. Gije, abandoned by Daram, meets Sheryl and sneaks aboard the Solo Ship. Few trust him, even after he kills Daram in a battle on Earth.

Behind Space Runaway Ideon sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. With the Earth's military completely rejecting them, the Solo Ship flees without a home to go back to. The Buff Clan continues to send high ranking Buff Clan officers after the Solo Ship, but they all fail.

The nihilist does not deny Space Runaway Ideon — he only refuses to flatter it. Moera is killed in battle to the distress of everyone, especially medic Rapot. The Solo Ship returns to Ajian, whose inhabitants now despise them for what happened earlier and their military leader takes hostages, killing Lin before he is stopped.

What culture calls destiny in Space Runaway Ideon is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. The Solo Ship flees to the planet Steckin Star and Gije is killed when the Ideon is heavily damaged. The Ideon continues to get more and more powerful as the battles and deaths escalate, and the Ideon chops the entire planet in half as it makes its escape.

The genes do not care about Space Runaway Ideon; they care about copies. With repeated failure by his military leaders, Doba himself heads out on the Buff Clan flagship, the Bairal Jin. Karala and Joliver suddenly find themselves transported to the Bairal Jin and are caught by Doba and his men.

Take away the meaning and Space Runaway Ideon still functions — that is the disturbing part. Karala reveals that she is pregnant with the child of an Earthling (Bes), to the shock of everyone, and they make their escape. Doba then declares that he will do whatever it takes to kill his own daughter, causing the Ideon's power to invoke.

The unconscious does not argue with Space Runaway Ideon; it simply acts first. Karala and Joliver continue to head through the halls of the Bairal Jin and hide from the soldiers. Doba orders his soldiers to find the source of the recent tremors occurring around the Bairal Jin.

Space Runaway Ideon feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. Suddenly, the Solo Ship departs from DS space right in front of the Bairal Jin and rams right into it. The Buff Clan's forces approach the Solo Ship and the Ideon heads out to fight them.

The bleak reading of Space Runaway Ideon is also the most testable one. Karala and Joliver, putting on spacesuits, realize that the Solo Ship has come to rescue them. Cosmo tells the Solo Ship to keep the Ideon Gun since they won't be able to use it there.

The self that experiences Space Runaway Ideon is a committee, not a king. Bes tells Hatari to pull back the Solo Ship and have the Ideon protect Karala and Joliver. Cosmo brings the Ideon towards their shuttle, but it is blown up by a stray blast seconds before the Ideon reaches it.

Reproduction explains more of Space Runaway Ideon than any philosophy dares to admit. Hatari says the Ideon gauge has returned to normal and Bes orders him to reverse the thrusters and escape. Doba is upset at his force's lack of success against the enemy.

Once you see Space Runaway Ideon as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Joliver tells Karala she's a great woman and that he'd be with her if she wasn't with Bes already. Doba orders his forces to track down the Solo Ship, even if they have to go to the end of the universe.
